definition_zh: 父亲；祖先；神父；创始人
definition_en: a male parent, a male ancestor, a title for a priest, or the founder of something
core_image: 傍晚的院子里，父亲把孩子高高举过头顶，笑声惊起了树上的麻雀
scene: 傍晚的院子里，他把孩子举过头顶，笑声一直传到巷口。The father lifted his child high above his head.
sceneCN: 这里 father 是「父亲」（第 1 个义项）；句意：父亲把孩子高高举过头顶。

senses.title: A male parent
senses.definition: a man in relation to his child
senses.definitionCN: 与自己的孩子相对的男性家长
senses.example: His father taught him to swim.
senses.exampleCN: 他父亲教他游泳。
senses.why: The family sense is the oldest and most central use.
senses.whyCN: 家庭关系义是最古老、最核心的用法。

senses.title: A male ancestor
senses.definition: a man from whom a family or group is descended
senses.definitionCN: 家族或群体的男性先辈
senses.example: Their fathers came from the same village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的祖先来自同一个村庄。
senses.why: The parent sense stretches back along the family line.
senses.whyCN: 父亲义沿家族血脉向上延伸为祖先。

senses.title: A priest's title
senses.definition: a respectful title used for a priest
senses.definitionCN: 对神职人员的一种尊称
senses.example: Father John greeted the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 约翰神父迎接了来访者。
senses.why: Priests are addressed as fathers in the church tradition.
senses.whyCN: 教会传统中以父亲称呼神职人员。

senses.title: The founder of something
senses.definition: a person who starts or inspires a movement or field
senses.definitionCN: 开创或启发某项事业或领域的人
senses.example: He is called the father of the telephone.
senses.exampleCN: 他被称为电话之父。
senses.why: A founder stands at the beginning like a parent of the work.
senses.whyCN: 创始者像事业的家长一样站在起点上。

intro.en: Father goes back to Old English fæder and shares a very old root with many European languages.
intro.cn: father 可追溯到古英语 fæder，与许多欧洲语言共享一个非常古老的词根。

items.en: The root pəter named a father in the ancient ancestor language.
items.cn: 词根 pəter 在远古祖语中表示父亲。

items.en: The form fader carried the family sense into Germanic speech.
items.cn: fader 这一形式把家庭义带入日耳曼语。

items.en: Fæder was the everyday word for a male parent.
items.cn: fæder 是古英语中表示父亲的日常用词。

items.en: The spelling settled as fader and later father.
items.cn: 拼写先固定为 fader，后来变为 father。

items.en: Father also became a title for priests and a name for founders.
items.cn: 现代英语中 father 又成为神父的称呼和创始人的代称。

note.en: Father is compared with similar-looking words and with words for parents and ancestors.
note.cn: 把 father 与形近词以及表示父母、祖先的词作比较。

entries.definition: to a greater degree or distance
one of the light growths covering a bird
a person from whom one is descended

normalIntro.en: Father is the male parent, and the same word names priests and founders.
normalIntro.cn: father 是男性家长，同一个词也可指神父与创始人。

normal.en: Father and farther sound alike but mean different things.
normal.cn: father 与 farther 读音相近，但意思不同。

normal.en: Father Christmas is the British name for Santa Claus.
normal.cn: Father Christmas 是英式英语中对圣诞老人的称呼。

normal.en: A father figure is an older man who guides others.
normal.cn: father figure 指引导他人的年长男性。

normal.en: Fatherhood names the state of being a father.
normal.cn: fatherhood 指身为父亲的状态。

normal.en: Forefather adds fore to father to mean an ancestor.
normal.cn: forefather 在 father 前加 fore，表示祖先。

abstract.en: One word can name a parent, a priest, and a founder.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以同时指父亲、神父和创始人。

abstract.en: Kinship words often stretch toward honor and origin.
abstract.cn: 表示亲属的词常常延伸到敬意与起源。

abstract.en: Calling someone father is both a family tie and a sign of respect.
abstract.cn: 称某人为父亲既是家庭纽带，也是敬意。

examples.en: My father drives me to school every morning.
examples.cn: 我父亲每天早上开车送我上学。

examples.en: The visitors asked Father Thomas to lead the prayer.
examples.cn: 来访者请托马斯神父带领祈祷。

examples.en: She is regarded as the father of the project.
examples.cn: 她被视为这个项目的创始人。

dict_mnemonic.text: father 与德语 Vater 同源，都来自古代表示家庭男性长辈的词，核心是「一家之父」。

root: 源自原始印欧语 pəter（父亲），经日耳曼语与古英语 fæder，核心义「家庭中的男性长辈」。

sensesIntro.en: Father means a male parent, a male ancestor, a priest's title, or the founder of something.
sensesIntro.cn: father 意为父亲、男性祖先、神父的称呼，或某事物的创始人。

core.en: The male parent at the head of a family, and figures who take that role.
core.cn: 家庭中的男性家长，以及承担这一角色的形象。

branches.en: The man who raises a child.
A male ancestor in the family line.
branches.cn: 家族血脉中的男性祖先。

branches.en: A respectful title for a priest.
The person who begins or inspires something.
Both the parent and the founder stand at the beginning of a line.
branches.cn: 父亲与创始人都站在某条脉络的起点。

intro.en: Father forms words for family roles, family states, and compound kinship terms.
intro.cn: father 构成表示家庭角色、身份状态与复合亲属称谓的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: Her father works in a hospital.
items.exampleCN: 她父亲在一家医院工作。

items.example: The fathers waited outside the classroom.
items.exampleCN: 父亲们在教室外等候。

items.example: He gave her fatherly advice.
items.exampleCN: 他给了她慈父般的建议。

items.meaning: the state of being a father
items.example: Fatherhood changed his daily habits.
items.exampleCN: 成为父亲改变了他的日常习惯。

items.example: The fatherless boy was raised by his aunt.
items.exampleCN: 这个没有父亲的男孩由姑妈抚养长大。

items.example: My grandfather tells old stories.
items.exampleCN: 我祖父会讲古老的故事。

items.meaning: a man who marries one's mother
items.example: Her stepfather taught her to ride a bike.
items.exampleCN: 她的继父教她骑自行车。

items.example: The forefathers of the town built the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 这座小镇的祖先修建了那座桥。

items.example: He returned to his fatherland after years abroad.
items.exampleCN: 在国外多年后，他回到了祖国。

definition_zh: 疲劳；劳累；使疲劳；金属疲劳
definition_en: extreme tiredness, the act of making someone tired, or the weakening of metal under repeated stress
core_image: 深夜的办公室里，他揉着眼睛站起来，桌上的咖啡杯已经空了好几次
scene: 连续加班好几天后，他坐在椅子上连手都抬不起来。Fatigue made every step feel heavy.
sceneCN: 这里 fatigue 是「疲劳」（第 1 个义项）；句意：疲劳让每一步都变得沉重。

senses.title: Extreme tiredness
senses.definition: a state of being extremely tired in body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 身体或精神极度疲惫的状态
senses.example: The long march left the soldiers in deep fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 长途行军让士兵们疲惫不堪。
senses.why: This is the central everyday sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词最核心的日常含义。

senses.title: To make someone tired
senses.definition: to cause a person or body to become extremely tired
senses.definitionCN: 使人或身体变得极度疲惫
senses.example: The night shift fatigues workers quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班很快就会让工人疲惫。
senses.why: The noun sense turns into a verb of causing tiredness.
senses.whyCN: 名词义转化为表示「使人疲倦」的动词。

senses.title: Weakness in metal
senses.definition: the weakening of metal caused by repeated stress
senses.definitionCN: 金属因反复受力而变弱的现象
senses.example: Engineers checked the wing for metal fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师检查机翼是否有金属疲劳。
senses.why: The idea of tiredness is applied to materials under stress.
senses.whyCN: 把「疲劳」的观念用于承受压力的材料。

senses.title: A duty or chore
senses.definition: a task or duty, especially an unpleasant military one
senses.definitionCN: 任务或勤务，尤指军中杂役
senses.example: He was put on kitchen fatigue.
senses.exampleCN: 他被派去厨房做杂役。
senses.why: A separate military sense names tiring routine work.
senses.whyCN: 另一个军事义项指令人劳累的日常杂务。

intro.en: Fatigue came into English from French, ultimately from the Latin verb fatigare, to tire out.
intro.cn: fatigue 经法语进入英语，最终源自拉丁语动词 fatigare（使疲惫）。

items.en: Fatigare meant to tire out or wear down.
items.cn: fatigare 意为使筋疲力尽或消耗。

items.en: The noun fatigue named weariness and hard labor.
items.cn: 古法语名词 fatigue 表示疲倦与苦役。

items.en: Fatigue entered English as a word for extreme weariness.
items.cn: fatigue 以「极度疲倦」之义进入英语。

items.en: Military writers used fatigue for tiring routine duties.
items.cn: 军事作家用 fatigue 指令人疲劳的日常勤务。

items.en: Engineers borrowed the word for weakness in stressed metal.
items.cn: 工程师借这个词表示受应力金属的弱化。

note.en: Fatigue is compared with similar-looking words and with words for tiredness.
note.cn: 把 fatigue 与形近词以及表示疲倦的词作比较。

entries.definition: a death caused by an accident or disaster
the feeling of being very tired

normalIntro.en: Fatigue is deep tiredness, and the same word describes tired metal.
normalIntro.cn: fatigue 是极度疲惫，同一个词也用来描述金属的疲劳。

normal.en: Fatigue is stronger than ordinary tiredness.
normal.cn: fatigue 比普通的 tiredness 程度更重。

normal.en: Metal fatigue names cracks caused by repeated stress.
normal.cn: metal fatigue 指反复受力造成的裂纹。

normal.en: The verb fatigue means to wear someone out.
normal.cn: 动词 fatigue 意为使某人筋疲力尽。

normal.en: Indefatigable means never getting tired.
normal.cn: indefatigable 意为不知疲倦的。

normal.en: Fatigue duty is tiring routine work.
normal.cn: fatigue duty 指令人劳累的杂务。

abstract.en: Tiredness of the body became a way to describe tiredness of metal.
abstract.cn: 身体的疲惫被用来描述金属的疲劳。

abstract.en: Hard labor links the senses of weariness and duty.
abstract.cn: 艰苦劳作把疲惫与勤务两个义项联系起来。

abstract.en: A word for exhaustion can also name what causes it.
abstract.cn: 表示疲惫的词也可以指造成疲惫的事物。

examples.en: The heat and long hours brought on fatigue.
examples.cn: 炎热和长时间工作引发了疲劳。

examples.en: The steep climb fatigued even the strongest hikers.
examples.cn: 陡峭的山路让最强壮的徒步者都疲惫不堪。

examples.en: Metal fatigue can cause sudden cracks in a bridge.
examples.cn: 金属疲劳可能使桥梁突然开裂。

dict_mnemonic.text: fatigue 源自拉丁语 fatigare（使疲惫），经法语 fatigue 进入英语，含义从「劳作过度」扩展到「金属疲劳」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fatigare（使疲惫），经法语 fatigue 传入，核心义「因过度劳累而衰弱」。

sensesIntro.en: Fatigue means extreme tiredness, the act of tiring someone, weakness in metal, or a tiring duty.
sensesIntro.cn: fatigue 意为极度疲劳、使人疲惫、金属疲劳，或令人劳累的勤务。

core.en: A heavy loss of energy caused by long or hard effort.
core.cn: 因长期或艰苦付出而造成的精力严重损耗。

branches.en: The state of being extremely tired.
The act of making someone tired.
Weakness caused by stress in metal.
branches.cn: 金属受应力后产生的弱化。

branches.en: A tiring routine duty.
Feeling tired and causing tiredness are two sides of one process.
branches.cn: 感到疲惫与使人疲惫是同一过程的两个方面。

intro.en: Fatigue builds words for tiredness, for resistance to tiredness, and for extreme weariness.
intro.cn: fatigue 构成表示疲惫、抗疲劳与极度劳累的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fatigare and its noun fatigatio supply the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fatigare 及其名词 fatigatio 提供历史词根。

items.meaning: extreme tiredness or to tire out
items.example: Fatigue slowed the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 疲劳拖慢了整个团队。

items.example: The soldiers wore their fatigues.
items.exampleCN: 士兵们穿着作训服。

items.example: The crew looked fatigued after the flight.
items.exampleCN: 机组人员在飞行后显得很疲惫。

items.example: It was a fatiguing day of travel.
items.exampleCN: 那是令人疲惫的一天旅途。

items.example: Long training can overfatigue young players.
items.exampleCN: 长时间训练会使年轻球员过度疲劳。

items.example: The mat has an antifatigue surface.
items.exampleCN: 这块垫子有抗疲劳表面。

items.example: She was an indefatigable researcher.
items.exampleCN: 她是一位不知疲倦的研究者。

items.example: He worked indefatigably on the project.
items.exampleCN: 他不知疲倦地投入这个项目。

latinEntries.meaning: to tire out or wear down

latinEntries.example: Fatigatio names a state of weariness.

definition_zh: 水龙头；旋塞；出水口
definition_en: a device that controls the flow of water from a pipe, its valve, or the spout where the water comes out
core_image: 厨房水槽上方的金属龙头，一滴水正挂在出水口，久久没有落下
scene: 他拧开水龙头，接了一杯凉水。She turned the faucet and filled a glass with cold water.
sceneCN: 这里 faucet 是「水龙头」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她拧开水龙头，接了一杯凉水。

senses.title: A water tap
senses.definition: a device that lets water out of a pipe when opened
senses.definitionCN: 打开后能让水从管道流出的装置
senses.example: The kitchen faucet is dripping again.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的水龙头又滴水了。
senses.why: This is the common American sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是该词在美式英语中最常见的含义。

senses.title: A valve controlling flow
senses.definition: the valve inside such a device that opens or closes the flow
senses.definitionCN: 装置内部控制水流开闭的阀门
senses.example: Turn the faucet clockwise to shut off the water.
senses.exampleCN: 顺时针转动旋塞就能关掉水。
senses.why: The visible handle works a valve, and the word names both.
senses.whyCN: 可见的把手操控阀门，而该词同时指称两者。

senses.title: The water outlet
senses.definition: the spout or outlet where water leaves the pipe
senses.definitionCN: 水离开管道的喷嘴或出口
senses.example: She held the cup under the faucet.
senses.exampleCN: 她把杯子放在出水口下方。
senses.why: The part people see and use most is the spout itself.
senses.whyCN: 人们最常看到和使用的部分就是出水口。

intro.en: Faucet comes from Old French fausset, a bung or stopper, probably linked to faux, false.
intro.cn: faucet 源自表示塞子的古法语 fausset，可能和 faux（虚假的）有关。

items.en: Falsus meant false or deceptive.
items.cn: falsus 意为虚假的、骗人的。

items.en: Fausset named a bung used to stop a cask.
items.cn: fausset 指用来塞住木桶的塞子。

items.en: The word crossed into English use for a pipe stopper.
items.cn: 该词传入英语，指管道塞子。

items.en: Faucet named a tap or spout for liquid.
items.cn: faucet 指放出液体的龙头或喷嘴。

items.en: American English made faucet the everyday word for a tap.
items.cn: 美式英语中 faucet 成为水龙头的日常说法。

note.en: Faucet is compared with similar-looking words and with words for taps and valves.
note.cn: 把 faucet 与形近词以及表示龙头、阀门的词作比较。

entries.definition: one side or aspect of something
the passage at the back of the mouth
a device for controlling water, used in British English
a small tap or stopper for a barrel
a part that controls the flow of liquid or gas

normalIntro.en: Faucet is the American word for a tap and the valve behind it.
normalIntro.cn: faucet 是美式英语中的水龙头，也指其内部阀门。

normal.en: British speakers usually say tap instead of faucet.
normal.cn: 英国人通常说 tap，而不是 faucet。

normal.en: A dripping faucet wastes water.
normal.cn: 滴水的龙头会浪费水。

normal.en: Faucet and facet differ by one letter.
normal.cn: faucet 和 facet 只差一个字母。

normal.en: Turn the faucet off after washing your hands.
normal.cn: 洗完手后要关掉水龙头。

normal.en: The hot faucet carries water from the heater.
normal.cn: 热水龙头输送来自热水器的水。

abstract.en: A stopper became a spout as plumbing changed.
abstract.cn: 随着管道技术进步，塞子变成了出水口。

abstract.en: One fixture holds a handle, a valve, and an outlet.
abstract.cn: 一件龙头装置同时包含把手、阀门与出水口。

abstract.en: American and British words can split one simple object.
abstract.cn: 美式与英式说法会把同一个简单物件分成两个词。

examples.en: The faucet in the bathroom leaks.
examples.cn: 浴室的水龙头漏水。

examples.en: Please turn off the faucet after use.
examples.cn: 用完后请关掉水龙头。

examples.en: A plumber replaced the old faucet.
examples.cn: 水管工换掉了旧龙头。

dict_mnemonic.text: faucet 经古法语 fausset（塞子）进入英语，最初指管道的塞子，后来专指控制水流的水龙头。

root: 源自拉丁语 falsus（虚假的）经古法语 fausset（塞子），核心义「控制管道水流的装置」。

sensesIntro.en: Faucet means a water tap, the valve that controls it, or the spout where water comes out.
sensesIntro.cn: faucet 意为水龙头、控制水流的阀门，或出水的喷嘴。

core.en: A household device that starts and stops the flow of water.
core.cn: 控制水流开启与关闭的家用装置。

branches.en: The whole fixture people turn on and off.
branches.cn: 人们开关的整套龙头装置。

branches.en: The inner valve that controls the flow.
The spout where the water leaves.
The fixture and its outlet are seen as one object.
branches.cn: 装置与出水口被视为同一个物件。

branches.en: Turning the fixture means working the valve inside.
branches.cn: 转动龙头就是操作内部的阀门。

intro.en: Faucet has few derived forms, so related plumbing words fill out the family.
intro.cn: faucet 的派生形式很少，因此用相关管道词汇补足词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin falsus and Old French fausset stand behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 falsus 与古法语 fausset 是该词的历史来源。

items.example: The faucet is beside the sink.
items.exampleCN: 水龙头在水槽旁边。

items.example: The hotel replaced all the faucets.
items.exampleCN: 酒店更换了所有水龙头。

items.meaning: the British word for a faucet
items.example: Turn the tap to the left.
items.exampleCN: 把龙头向左转。

items.example: The old taps were made of brass.
items.exampleCN: 旧龙头是黄铜做的。

items.example: He opened the spigot on the barrel.
items.exampleCN: 他打开了木桶上的龙头。

items.example: The pipes end in brass spigots.
items.exampleCN: 管道末端装着黄铜龙头。

items.example: The valve must be closed first.
items.exampleCN: 必须先关闭阀门。

items.example: The plumber checked both valves.
items.exampleCN: 水管工检查了两个阀门。

definition_zh: 错误；过失；故障；断层
definition_en: a mistake, the blame for something wrong, a defect in a machine or system, or a break in rock layers
core_image: 工程师蹲在机器旁，手电筒照着烧焦的线路接头，眉头越皱越紧
scene: 机器突然停了，工程师顺着线路找到了烧坏的地方。A fault in the wiring stopped the machine.
sceneCN: 这里 fault 是「故障」（第 3 个义项）；句意：线路故障让机器停了下来。

senses.title: A mistake
senses.definition: something done wrongly or a flaw in what was done
senses.definitionCN: 做错的事或做好之事中的疏漏
senses.example: The report contained several faults.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告有几处错误。
senses.why: This is the broad everyday sense of something wrong.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「失误」的宽泛日常义。

senses.title: Blame or responsibility
senses.definition: responsibility for something bad that happened
senses.definitionCN: 对发生的坏事所负的责任
senses.example: The accident was not his fault.
senses.exampleCN: 这场事故不是他的过错。
senses.why: A fault is often the basis for assigning blame.
senses.whyCN: 过错常常是追究责任的依据。

senses.title: A defect or breakdown
senses.definition: a defect in a machine, system, or person
senses.definitionCN: 机器、系统或人身上的缺陷
senses.example: A fault cut the power to the whole street.
senses.exampleCN: 一场故障让整条街都停了电。
senses.why: A mistake in a device becomes a technical fault.
senses.whyCN: 设备中的失误就成了技术故障。

senses.title: A break in rock
senses.definition: a crack in rock where the two sides have moved
senses.definitionCN: 岩层中两侧发生位移的裂缝
senses.example: The earthquake happened along a known fault.
senses.exampleCN: 地震发生在一条已知断层上。
senses.why: Geologists borrowed the word for a break in the earth.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家借这个词表示岩层的断裂。

intro.en: Fault came through Old French faute from Latin fallere, to deceive or fail.
intro.cn: fault 经古法语 faute 传入，源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失误）。

items.en: Fallere meant to deceive, trick, or cause to fail.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗、蒙骗或使失败。

items.en: A popular noun form described a failure or defect.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁语中用名词形式表示失误或缺陷。

items.en: Faute meant a lack, mistake, or offense.
items.cn: faute 意为缺失、错误或冒犯。

items.en: Fault entered English with the sense of a mistake.
items.cn: fault 以「错误」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word added senses of machine defects and rock breaks.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了机械故障与岩层断层的义项。

note.en: Fault is compared with similar-looking words and with words for mistakes and defects.
note.cn: 把 fault 与形近词以及表示错误、缺陷的词作比较。

entries.definition: a curved roof or a secure room
a failure to do something required
an action or opinion that is wrong
a fault or weakness in something
a mistake, especially in writing or calculation

normalIntro.en: A fault is a mistake, the blame for it, a defect, or a break in rock.
normalIntro.cn: fault 指错误、应有的责任、缺陷，或岩层断层。

normal.en: Be at fault means to be responsible for a problem.
normal.cn: be at fault 意为对某个问题负有责任。

normal.en: To find fault with someone is to criticize them.
normal.cn: find fault with 某人意为挑剔对方。

normal.en: A fault line marks a crack in the earth.
normal.cn: fault line 标出地壳中的断裂带。

normal.en: Faulty adds -y to fault to mean full of faults.
normal.cn: faulty 由 fault 加 -y 构成，意为有缺陷的。

normal.en: A technical fault is a problem in a device.
normal.cn: technical fault 指设备中出现的问题。

abstract.en: A small mistake can grow into legal blame.
abstract.cn: 小失误可能演变为法律责任。

abstract.en: The same word covers a bad wire and a broken rock layer.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指坏掉的电线，也指断裂的岩层。

abstract.en: Naming a fault is often the first step to repair.
abstract.cn: 指出缺陷往往是修复的第一步。

examples.en: The engineers found a fault in the pump.
examples.cn: 工程师在泵里发现了一处故障。

examples.en: It was my fault that we were late.
examples.cn: 我们迟到是我的过错。

examples.en: The valley lies on a major fault.
examples.cn: 这条山谷位于一条主要断层上。

dict_mnemonic.text: fault 源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失误），经古法语 faute 传入，词义从「失误」扩展到「责任」与「故障」。

root: 源自拉丁语 fallere（欺骗、失败），经古法语 faute，核心义「失误及其造成的缺陷与责任」。

sensesIntro.en: Fault means a mistake, blame for something, a defect in a machine, or a crack in rock.
sensesIntro.cn: fault 意为错误、应负的责任、机器缺陷，或岩层断层。

core.en: A failure or defect, together with the blame it brings.
core.cn: 失败或缺陷，以及由此产生的责任。

branches.en: Something done wrongly.
Responsibility for what went wrong.
A defect that stops a device working.
branches.cn: 使设备无法运转的缺陷。

branches.en: A break where rock layers have moved.
A mistake and the blame for it travel together.
branches.cn: 错误与由此而来的责任总是相伴。

intro.en: Fault forms words for defects, perfection, and the habit of finding blame.
intro.cn: fault 构成表示缺陷、完美以及挑剔习惯的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere and the popular noun fallita are the deeper sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 与通俗拉丁语名词 fallita 是更深的来源。

items.meaning: a mistake, defect, or to criticize
items.example: The fault was soon repaired.
items.exampleCN: 故障很快修好了。

items.example: The inspector listed three faults.
items.exampleCN: 检查员列出了三处缺陷。

items.example: The rock is faulted along the ridge.
items.exampleCN: 山脊沿线的岩层有断层。

items.meaning: the act of criticizing or forming faults
items.example: Constant faulting damaged their friendship.
items.exampleCN: 不断挑剔损害了他们的友谊。

items.example: The faulty switch was replaced.
items.exampleCN: 有故障的开关被换掉了。

items.example: She gave a faultless performance.
items.exampleCN: 她的表演无可挑剔。

items.example: He answered faultlessly.
items.exampleCN: 他完美地回答了问题。

items.example: Tests revealed the faultiness of the design.
items.exampleCN: 测试揭示了设计的缺陷。

items.meaning: the habit of looking for mistakes
items.example: His faultfinding upset the team.
items.exampleCN: 他的挑剔让团队不快。

items.example: The loan went into default.
items.exampleCN: 这笔贷款出现了违约。

latinEntries.meaning: to deceive or cause to fail

definition_zh: 有故障的；有缺陷的；错误的
definition_en: not working properly, having a flaw, or based on a mistaken idea
core_image: 天花板上的灯一闪一闪，电工拆开开关，看见一根松动的接线
scene: 灯闪了几下就灭了，问题出在一根接错的电线上。A faulty wire made the lights flicker.
sceneCN: 这里 faulty 是「有故障的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一根有故障的电线让灯闪烁。

senses.title: Not working properly
senses.definition: not working correctly because of a defect
senses.definitionCN: 因缺陷而无法正常运转
senses.example: The faulty printer jammed twice.
senses.exampleCN: 那台有故障的打印机卡了两次纸。
senses.why: This is the most common everyday use for machines.
senses.whyCN: 这是描述机器时最常见的日常用法。

senses.title: Having a flaw
senses.definition: having a weakness or flaw in design or structure
senses.definitionCN: 设计或结构上存在弱点或瑕疵
senses.example: The plan rested on faulty assumptions.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划建立在有缺陷的假设上。
senses.why: The sense extends from machines to ideas and designs.
senses.whyCN: 该义从机器延伸到想法与设计。

senses.title: Based on a mistake
senses.definition: based on a mistaken judgment or memory
senses.definitionCN: 建立在错误判断或记忆之上
senses.example: His faulty memory confused the dates.
senses.exampleCN: 他不可靠的记忆把日期弄混了。
senses.why: Human judgment can be faulty in the same way as a device.
senses.whyCN: 人的判断也可能像设备一样出故障。

intro.en: Faulty was formed in English from fault, which came from Latin fallere through Old French.
intro.cn: faulty 由 fault 在英语中加后缀构成，而 fault 经古法语源自拉丁语 fallere。

items.en: Fallere meant to deceive or cause to fail.
items.cn: fallere 意为欺骗或使失败。

items.en: Faute named a mistake or lack.
items.cn: faute 表示错误或缺失。

items.en: Fault entered English as a word for a mistake.
items.cn: fault 以「错误」之义进入英语。

items.en: Faulty appeared as an adjective meaning full of faults.
items.cn: faulty 作为形容词出现，意为充满缺陷的。

items.en: The word now describes machines, arguments, and memory.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词可形容机器、论证与记忆。

note.en: Faulty is compared with similar-looking words and with words for defects.
note.cn: 把 faulty 与形近词以及表示缺陷的词作比较。

entries.definition: a natural ability or a university department
a mistaken belief or false argument

normalIntro.en: Faulty means full of faults, whether in a machine, a plan, or a memory.
normalIntro.cn: faulty 意为带有缺陷，无论指机器、计划还是记忆。

normal.en: Faulty adds -y to fault, just like health and healthy.
normal.cn: faulty 由 fault 加 -y 构成，正如 health 变 healthy。

normal.en: Faulty wiring is a common cause of fires.
normal.cn: 有故障的线路是火灾的常见原因。

normal.en: Faulty goods can be returned to the shop.
normal.cn: 有质量问题的商品可以退回商店。

normal.en: Faulty reasoning means the logic has a flaw.
normal.cn: faulty reasoning 指逻辑存在漏洞。

normal.en: Faulty hearing is not the same as deafness.
normal.cn: 听力有缺陷与完全失聪并不相同。

abstract.en: A machine, an argument, and a memory can all break in the same way.
abstract.cn: 机器、论证与记忆都可能以相似的方式出问题。

abstract.en: Calling something faulty points to a defect, not to blame.
abstract.cn: 说某物 faulty 是在指出缺陷，而非追究责任。

abstract.en: Faultless is the opposite picture of perfect working order.
abstract.cn: faultless 呈现的是完美运转的反面图景。

examples.en: The faulty heater gave off a strange smell.
examples.cn: 有故障的取暖器散发出怪味。

examples.en: Their faulty reasoning led to a poor choice.
examples.cn: 他们错误的推理导致了糟糕的选择。

examples.en: He replaced the faulty part with a new one.
examples.cn: 他用新零件替换了有故障的零件。

dict_mnemonic.text: faulty 由 fault（失误、缺陷）加形容词后缀 -y 构成，表示「带有缺陷的」。

root: 由 fault 加形容词后缀 -y 构成；fault 源自拉丁语 fallere（失误），核心义「带着缺陷的」。

sensesIntro.en: Faulty means not working properly, having a flaw, or based on a mistaken idea.
sensesIntro.cn: faulty 意为运转不正常、存在缺陷，或建立在错误想法上。

core.en: Something that contains a defect and therefore cannot be trusted.
core.cn: 含有缺陷、因而不可信赖的事物。

branches.en: A device that will not work correctly.
A plan or structure with a weakness.
branches.cn: 存在弱点的计划或结构。

branches.en: A judgment built on a mistake.
branches.cn: 建立在错误之上的判断。

branches.en: A bad wire and a bad memory both mislead us.
branches.cn: 坏掉的电线与不可靠的记忆都会误导我们。

branches.en: The defect may be in the working part or in the design.
branches.cn: 缺陷可能出现在运转部件，也可能出在设计上。

intro.en: Faulty belongs to a family built on fault with suffixes of defect and perfection.
intro.cn: faulty 属于以 fault 为核心、由缺陷与完美两类后缀构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fallere and fallita lie behind fault and faulty.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fallere 与 fallita 是 fault 和 faulty 的深层来源。

items.example: The fault was found in minutes.
items.exampleCN: 几分钟就找到了故障。

items.example: The old machine has many faults.
items.exampleCN: 这台旧机器有许多毛病。

items.example: The faulty cable was cut out.
items.exampleCN: 有故障的电缆被剪掉了。

items.example: This unit is faultier than the last.
items.exampleCN: 这台设备比上一台毛病更多。

items.example: That was the faultiest batch we tested.
items.exampleCN: 那是我们测试过问题最多的一批。

items.example: The engine ran faultily.
items.exampleCN: 发动机运转不正常。

items.example: The test measured the faultiness of the seal.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测量密封件的缺陷程度。

items.example: The copy was faultless.
items.exampleCN: 这份副本毫无差错。

items.meaning: the state of having no faults
items.example: No one expects faultlessness in a first draft.
items.exampleCN: 没人指望初稿毫无瑕疵。

definition_zh: 恩惠；帮忙；赞成；偏爱
definition_en: a kind act that helps someone, approval or support, or a preference shown to one side
core_image: 邻居隔着一道矮墙递来一篮刚摘的苹果，笑着说不用还
scene: 她帮邻居照看了一整天狗，邻居连声道谢。He asked me to do him a favour.
sceneCN: 这里 favour 是「恩惠；帮忙」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他请我帮他一个忙。

senses.title: A kind act
senses.definition: an act of kindness that helps another person
senses.definitionCN: 帮助他人的善意举动
senses.example: She did me a great favour last week.
senses.exampleCN: 她上周帮了我一个大忙。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a helpful act.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示「帮忙」的日常核心义。

senses.title: Approval or support
senses.definition: approval of or support for a plan or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对计划或想法的赞同与支持
senses.example: Most voters are in favour of the change.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数选民赞成这项改变。
senses.why: To favour something is to look on it with approval.
senses.whyCN: favour 某事物就是对其抱赞同态度。

senses.title: Partiality
senses.definition: unfair support shown to one person or group
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某群体给予的不公平支持
senses.example: The coach showed favour to his old players.
senses.exampleCN: 教练偏袒他的老队员。
senses.why: Approval can slide into unfair preference.
senses.whyCN: 赞同可能滑向不公平的偏好。

senses.title: To prefer or support
senses.definition: to prefer one thing or to support a plan
senses.definitionCN: 偏爱某事物或支持某项计划
senses.example: The committee favours a later start.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会倾向于较晚开始。
senses.why: The noun sense becomes a verb of choosing sides.
senses.whyCN: 名词义转化为表示选择立场的动词。

intro.en: Favour comes from Latin favere, to be kind or show good will, through Old French.
intro.cn: favour 经古法语传入，源自拉丁语 favere（善待、表示好意）。

items.en: Favere meant to be well disposed toward someone.
items.cn: favere 意为对某人心怀善意。

items.en: Favur named kindness and good will.
items.cn: favur 表示善意与好意。

items.en: Favour entered English as a word for a kind act.
items.cn: favour 以「善举」之义进入英语。

items.en: The spelling favour settled in British English.
items.cn: 英式英语中固定了 favour 这一拼写。

items.en: The word also means approval and unfair partiality.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词还表示赞同与不公平的偏袒。

note.en: Favour is compared with similar-looking words and with words for kindness and approval.
note.cn: 把 favour 与形近词以及表示好意、赞同的词作比较。

entries.definition: the taste of a food or drink
a greater liking for one thing

normalIntro.en: A favour is a kind act, and to favour is to prefer or support.
normalIntro.cn: favour 是善意的帮助，作动词则表示偏爱或支持。

normal.en: Do me a favour is a polite request for help.
normal.cn: do me a favour 是请人帮忙的礼貌说法。

normal.en: In favour of means supporting an idea.
normal.cn: in favour of 意为支持某个想法。

normal.en: Curry favour means to seek someone's approval.
normal.cn: curry favour 意为讨好某人以求得认可。

normal.en: Favouritism is unfair preference for one person.
normal.cn: favouritism 指对某人的不公平偏袒。

normal.en: British spelling keeps the u in favour.
normal.cn: 英式拼写 favour 保留了字母 u。

abstract.en: A small act of help can become a lasting debt of gratitude.
abstract.cn: 一次小小的帮助可能变成长久的感激。

abstract.en: Approval and bias grow from the same root of good will.
abstract.cn: 赞同与偏见都源自同一种好意的根。

abstract.en: Favouring one side always means another side loses.
abstract.cn: 偏爱一方总意味着另一方有所失去。

examples.en: Could you do me a favour and close the window?
examples.cn: 你能帮我个忙，把窗户关上吗？

examples.en: Most members were in favour of the plan.
examples.cn: 大多数成员赞成这个计划。

examples.en: The judge must not show favour to either side.
examples.cn: 法官不得偏袒任何一方。

dict_mnemonic.text: favour 源自拉丁语 favere（善待、支持），经古法语 favur 进入英语，核心含义是「善意与支持」。

root: 源自拉丁语 favere（善待、支持），经古法语 favur，核心义「善意及其表现」。

sensesIntro.en: Favour means a kind act, approval, unfair partiality, or to prefer and support.
sensesIntro.cn: favour 意为善意的帮助、赞同、不公平的偏袒，或偏爱与支持。

core.en: Good will shown to someone, whether through help or preference.
core.cn: 对他人表现出的好意，无论是帮助还是偏爱。

branches.en: A helpful act done for someone.
Support for a plan or idea.
Unfair preference for one side.
To choose or support something.
A kind act and open approval both express good will.
branches.cn: 善意之举与公开赞同都表达好意。

intro.en: Favour builds words for approval, preference, and unfair bias.
intro.cn: favour 构成表示赞同、偏爱与不公平偏袒的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin favere and its noun favor supply the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 favere 及其名词 favor 提供历史词根。

items.meaning: a kind act or to prefer
items.example: He did her a small favour.
items.exampleCN: 他帮了她一个小忙。

items.example: She never forgets favours done to her.
items.exampleCN: 她从不忘记别人给她的帮助。

items.example: The favoured route avoids the city.
items.exampleCN: 受青睐的路线避开市区。

items.example: The report was accused of favouring one firm.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告被指责偏袒某一家公司。

items.example: The reply was favourable.
items.exampleCN: 答复是赞成的。

items.meaning: in a helpful or approving way
items.example: The plan was received favourably.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划受到了欢迎。

items.example: This is my favourite seat.
items.exampleCN: 这是我最喜欢的座位。

items.example: The manager was accused of favouritism.
items.exampleCN: 经理被指控偏袒。

items.example: The weather turned unfavourable.
items.exampleCN: 天气变得不利。

items.example: The plan had few favourers.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划支持者寥寥。

latinEntries.meaning: to be kind or show good will
latinEntries.example: Favere means to show good will.

definition_zh: 有利的；赞同的；讨人喜欢的
definition_en: helpful or advantageous, showing approval, or giving a good impression
core_image: 帆船离岸那天风向正好，船头轻轻切开平静的海面
scene: 天气预报说风向合适，正是出海的好日子。The weather was favourable for sailing.
sceneCN: 这里 favourable 是「有利的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：天气对航行有利。

pos.zh: 讨人喜欢的；给人好印象的

senses.title: Helpful or advantageous
senses.definition: making success more likely or conditions better
senses.definitionCN: 使成功更有可能或使条件更好
senses.example: The conditions were favourable for an early start.
senses.exampleCN: 条件有利于尽早出发。
senses.why: This is the main sense in weather and planning.
senses.whyCN: 这是天气与计划语境中的主要含义。

senses.title: Showing approval
senses.definition: expressing a positive opinion or agreement
senses.definitionCN: 表达正面看法或同意
senses.example: The committee gave a favourable response.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会给出了赞同的回应。
senses.why: A favourable reply carries approval.
senses.whyCN: favourable 的答复意味着赞同。

senses.title: Giving a good impression
senses.titleCN: 讨人喜欢的；给人好印象的
senses.definition: pleasing and likely to create a good opinion
senses.definitionCN: 令人满意、容易赢得良好评价的
senses.example: She made a favourable impression on the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 她给评审组留下了好印象。
senses.why: The sense moves from useful conditions to pleasing qualities.
senses.whyCN: 该义从有利条件转向讨人喜欢的品质。

intro.en: Favourable comes from Latin favorabilis, through Old French favorable.
intro.cn: favourable 源自拉丁语 favorabilis，经古法语 favorable 传入英语。

items.en: Favorabilis meant deserving or showing favor.
items.cn: favorabilis 意为值得青睐或表示好意的。

items.en: Favorable described something kind or helpful.
items.cn: favorable 形容善意或有利的事物。

items.en: The word entered English as a term for helpful conditions.
items.cn: 该词以「有利条件」之义进入英语。

items.en: British spelling settled as favourable with a u.
items.cn: 英式拼写固定为带 u 的 favourable。

items.en: The word now also describes approving replies and good impressions.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也形容赞同的答复与良好印象。

note.en: Favourable is compared with similar-looking words and with words for advantage.
note.cn: 把 favourable 与形近词以及表示有利的词作比较。

entries.definition: in a helpful or approving way

normalIntro.en: Favourable describes conditions that help, replies that approve, and qualities that please.
normalIntro.cn: favourable 形容有利的条件、赞同的答复与讨人喜欢的品质。

normal.en: Favourable weather makes a voyage easier.
normal.cn: 有利的天气让航行更轻松。

normal.en: A favourable reply says yes in a polite way.
normal.cn: favourable 的答复是以礼貌方式表示同意。

normal.en: A favourable impression often opens a door.
normal.cn: 好印象常常能打开一扇门。

normal.en: The opposite is unfavourable, with un- at the front.
normal.cn: 反义词是 unfavourable，在前面加 un-。

normal.en: American English drops the u and writes favorable.
normal.cn: 美式英语去掉 u，写作 favorable。

abstract.en: A wind can be favourable without being gentle.
abstract.cn: 有利的风未必是温和的风。

abstract.en: Conditions and opinions share one word because both can help or block.
abstract.cn: 条件与意见共用一个词，因为两者都能助人也能阻碍。

abstract.en: What pleases the eye is also what wins approval.
abstract.cn: 悦目之物也容易赢得赞同。

examples.en: The conditions were favourable for an early start.
examples.cn: 条件有利于尽早出发。

examples.en: She made a favourable impression on the panel.
examples.cn: 她给评审组留下了好印象。

examples.en: The reply was favourable and the deal went ahead.
examples.cn: 答复是赞同的，交易继续进行。

dict_mnemonic.text: favourable 由 favour 加 -able 构成，字面是「能带来好意的」，引申为「有利的、赞同的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 favorabilis（值得青睐的），经古法语 favorable，核心义「能带来帮助与好感的」。

sensesIntro.en: Favourable means helpful, approving, or pleasing enough to create a good impression.
sensesIntro.cn: favourable 意为有利的、赞同的，或讨人喜欢、能留下好印象的。

core.en: Something that works in your favour, whether conditions, replies, or looks.
core.cn: 对你有益的事物，无论是条件、答复还是外表。

branches.en: Conditions that make success easier.
A response that shows agreement.
A quality that wins a good opinion.
Both good weather and a good manner help you forward.
branches.cn: 好天气与好举止都有助于你前进。

branches.en: Helpful conditions and approving people often arrive together.
branches.cn: 有利条件与赞同的人常常一起出现。

intro.en: Favourable forms words for advantage, approval, and their opposites.
intro.cn: favourable 构成表示有利、赞同及其反面的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin favorabilis and favere are the historical sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 favorabilis 与 favere 是历史来源。

items.example: He asked for a small favour.
items.exampleCN: 他请求帮一个小忙。

items.example: The outlook is favourable.
items.exampleCN: 前景是有利的。

items.example: The plan was favourably received.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划受到好评。

items.example: They judged the favourableness of the soil.
items.exampleCN: 他们评估了土壤的适宜程度。

items.example: The ship waited out unfavourable winds.
items.exampleCN: 船等待不利的风过去。

items.example: The report compared the two plans unfavourably.
items.exampleCN: 报告把两个计划作了不利的比较。

items.example: Blue is her favourite colour.
items.exampleCN: 蓝色是她最喜欢的颜色。

items.example: The rules forbid favouritism.
items.exampleCN: 规则禁止偏袒。

items.example: The favoured candidate won.
items.exampleCN: 受青睐的候选人获胜了。

items.example: A favouring bias spoiled the test.
items.exampleCN: 偏袒倾向破坏了测试的公正。

definition_zh: 最喜爱的；最喜爱的人或物；宠儿
definition_en: liked best of all, the person or thing liked best, or someone given special treatment
core_image: 床头那本故事书被翻得起了毛边，书签还夹在最喜欢的一页
scene: 她每天睡前都要读同一本故事书，那是她的最爱。This is her favourite storybook.
sceneCN: 这里 favourite 是「最喜爱的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这是她最喜爱的故事书。

collocations.zh: 一直很受欢迎的人或物

senses.title: Liked best
senses.definition: liked more than all others of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 在同类别中最受喜爱的
senses.example: Pizza is his favourite food.
senses.exampleCN: 披萨是他最喜爱的食物。
senses.why: This is the everyday adjective sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最常用的形容词义。

senses.title: The one liked best
senses.definition: the person or thing that is liked best
senses.definitionCN: 最受喜爱的人或物
senses.example: The song became a favourite with young listeners.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌成了年轻听众的最爱。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the chosen one.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转化为名词，指被选中的人或物。

senses.title: A person shown special favour
senses.definition: someone treated with special kindness or preference
senses.definitionCN: 受到特别关照或偏爱之人
senses.example: She is the teacher's favourite.
senses.exampleCN: 她是老师偏爱的学生。
senses.why: Preference can become unfair special treatment.
senses.whyCN: 偏爱可能变成不公平的特殊照顾。

intro.en: Favourite comes from Latin favere through French favorit, meaning one who is favored.
intro.cn: favourite 经法语 favorit（受宠者）源自拉丁语 favere。

items.en: Favere meant to show kindness or support.
items.cn: favere 意为表示善意或支持。

items.en: Favorit named a person who enjoyed favor.
items.cn: favorit 指受到恩宠的人。

items.en: The sense widened to anything preferred.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何受偏爱的事物。

items.en: Favourite entered English as both noun and adjective.
items.cn: favourite 作为名词和形容词进入英语。

items.en: The word now covers food, songs, sports teams, and people.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词可指食物、歌曲、球队与人。

note.en: Favourite is compared with similar-looking words and with words for being preferred.
note.cn: 把 favourite 与形近词以及表示受偏爱的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Favourite marks the one you like best, whether a food, a song, or a person.
normalIntro.cn: favourite 标出你最喜欢的那一个，无论是食物、歌曲还是人。

normal.en: Favourite is spelled with a u in British English.
normal.cn: 英式英语中 favourite 带有字母 u。

normal.en: My favourite means the one I like most.
normal.cn: my favourite 意为「我的最爱」。

normal.en: A favourite can be a person as well as a thing.
normal.cn: favourite 既可以指物，也可以指人。

normal.en: Being the teacher's favourite can be awkward.
normal.cn: 成为老师偏爱的学生有时会很尴尬。

normal.en: Favouritism turns favourite into an unfair habit.
normal.cn: favouritism 把 favourite 变成不公平的偏袒。

abstract.en: Choosing a favourite is a small act of ranking the world.
abstract.cn: 选出一个最爱，是对世界做的一次小小排序。

abstract.en: What is liked best often says more about the chooser than the thing.
abstract.cn: 最喜爱之物往往更多说明选择者，而非事物本身。

abstract.en: Special favor can turn a favourite into an outsider among peers.
abstract.cn: 特殊偏爱可能让宠儿在同龄人中成为异类。

examples.en: Pizza is his favourite food.
examples.cn: 披萨是他最喜爱的食物。

examples.en: She is the teacher's favourite.
examples.cn: 她是老师偏爱的学生。

examples.en: The song became a favourite with young listeners.
examples.cn: 这首歌成了年轻听众的最爱。

dict_mnemonic.text: favourite 经法语 favorit（受宠者）进入英语，核心是「受到偏爱的那一个」。

root: 源自拉丁语 favere（偏爱、支持），经法语 favorit，核心义「最受喜爱的人或物」。

sensesIntro.en: Favourite means liked best, the one liked best, or a person given special favor.
sensesIntro.cn: favourite 意为最喜爱的、最喜爱的人或物，或受特别偏爱之人。

core.en: The person or thing that stands first in someone's affection.
core.cn: 在某人喜爱中排在第一位的人或物。

branches.en: The quality of being liked best.
The particular thing that is liked best.
A person who receives special treatment.
The adjective and the noun name the same preference.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词指称同一种偏爱。

branches.en: A beloved thing and a favored person share the spotlight.
branches.cn: 心爱之物与受宠之人共享聚光灯。

intro.en: Favourite belongs to the favour family and names preference and bias.
intro.cn: favourite 属于 favour 词族，表示偏爱与偏袒。

latinIntro.en: Latin favere and its noun favor stand behind the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 favere 及其名词 favor 是该词族的来源。

items.example: This is her favourite chair.
items.exampleCN: 这是她最喜欢的椅子。

items.example: The list has three favourites.
items.exampleCN: 名单上有三个最爱。

items.example: He did me a favour.
items.exampleCN: 他帮了我一个忙。

items.example: The favoured team won easily.
items.exampleCN: 被看好的球队轻松获胜。

items.example: The rules prevent favouring any group.
items.exampleCN: 规则禁止偏袒任何群体。

items.example: The news was favourable.
items.exampleCN: 消息是有利的。

items.example: She spoke favourably of the plan.
items.exampleCN: 她对计划表示赞许。

items.example: Favouritism undermines trust.
items.exampleCN: 偏袒会破坏信任。

items.example: They sailed against unfavourable winds.
items.exampleCN: 他们顶着不利的风航行。

items.example: The design was judged unfavourably.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计受到了负面评价。

definition_zh: 恐惧；害怕；担忧；敬畏
definition_en: the feeling caused by danger, worry about something, deep respect, or the verb to be afraid
core_image: 雷声在窗外炸开，孩子一把拽住被角，把自己整个裹了进去
scene: 深夜的雷声让孩子缩进被子里，连呼吸都放轻了。The loud thunder filled the child with fear.
sceneCN: 这里 fear 是「恐惧；害怕」（第 1 个义项）；句意：巨大的雷声让孩子充满恐惧。

senses.title: The feeling of danger
senses.definition: an unpleasant feeling caused by danger or threat
senses.definitionCN: 由危险或威胁引起的不快感受
senses.example: The dark forest filled her with fear.
senses.exampleCN: 黑暗的森林让她充满恐惧。
senses.why: This is the core emotional sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的情绪义。

senses.title: Worry or concern
senses.definition: a worry that something bad may happen
senses.definitionCN: 对可能发生坏事的担忧
senses.example: There is fear that prices will rise.
senses.exampleCN: 人们担心物价会上涨。
senses.why: Fear also covers milder anxiety about the future.
senses.whyCN: fear 也指对未来较轻的焦虑。

senses.title: Deep respect
senses.definition: a feeling of awe and respect, often toward nature or God
senses.definitionCN: 对自然或神灵等的敬畏之情
senses.example: They watched the storm with fear and wonder.
senses.exampleCN: 他们带着敬畏与惊奇观看风暴。
senses.why: Awe and dread can share one word.
senses.whyCN: 敬畏与恐惧可以共用同一个词。

senses.title: To be afraid
senses.definition: to feel afraid of something or worry that it will happen
senses.definitionCN: 害怕某事物或担心它发生
senses.example: He feared that the train would be late.
senses.exampleCN: 他担心火车会晚点。
senses.why: The noun sense becomes a verb of expectation.
senses.whyCN: 名词义转化为表示预感的动词。

intro.en: Fear comes from Old English fǣr, a sudden danger or calamity, from a Germanic root.
intro.cn: fear 源自古英语 fǣr（突如其来的危险或灾祸），出自日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root named sudden danger or a hostile attack.
items.cn: 该词根表示突发的危险或敌意袭击。

items.en: Fǣr meant a sudden calamity or peril.
items.cn: fǣr 意为突如其来的灾祸或危险。

items.en: Fere shifted from the danger itself to the feeling it caused.
items.cn: fere 从危险本身转向危险引起的感觉。

items.en: Fear became the standard word for the emotion.
items.cn: fear 成为表示这种情绪的标准词。

items.en: The word also expresses worry and religious awe.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词还表示担忧与宗教敬畏。

note.en: Fear is compared with similar-looking words and with words for strong anxiety.
note.cn: 把 fear 与形近词以及表示强烈焦虑的词作比较。

entries.definition: the money paid for a journey
a feeling of worry and unease

normalIntro.en: Fear is the feeling of danger, milder worry, deep awe, or the act of being afraid.
normalIntro.cn: fear 是面对危险的感觉、较轻的担忧、深深的敬畏，或害怕这一动作。

normal.en: For fear of means because you are afraid of something.
normal.cn: for fear of 意为因为害怕某事。

normal.en: Fear of heights is one of the most common fears.
normal.cn: 恐高是最常见的恐惧之一。

normal.en: Fearless means having no fear at all.
normal.cn: fearless 意为毫无畏惧。

normal.en: Fearsome describes something that causes fear.
normal.cn: fearsome 形容令人害怕的事物。

normal.en: The verb fear is often followed by that.
normal.cn: 动词 fear 后面常接 that 从句。

abstract.en: Fear began as the danger outside and moved inward to the feeling.
abstract.cn: fear 从外在的危险出发，转而指向内心的感受。

abstract.en: Awe and terror can share one word because both make us small.
abstract.cn: 敬畏与恐惧共用一个词，因为二者都让人自觉渺小。

abstract.en: Naming a fear is often the first step to facing it.
abstract.cn: 说出恐惧往往是面对它的第一步。

examples.en: She has a fear of deep water.
examples.cn: 她害怕深水。

examples.en: He feared that the train would be late.
examples.cn: 他担心火车会晚点。

examples.en: The villagers watched the storm with fear.
examples.cn: 村民们惊恐地看着风暴。

dict_mnemonic.text: fear 源自古英语 fǣr（突发的危险），词义由「危险本身」转为「危险带来的感受」。

root: 源自古英语 fǣr（突如其来的危险），出自日耳曼语词根，核心义「危险引发的恐惧」。

sensesIntro.en: Fear means the feeling of danger, worry, deep awe, or to be afraid of something.
sensesIntro.cn: fear 意为危险引起的恐惧、担忧、深深敬畏，或害怕某事物。

core.en: A strong response to danger, whether felt, feared, or revered.
core.cn: 对危险产生的强烈反应，无论是感受、担忧还是敬畏。

branches.en: The sharp emotion caused by danger.
A milder worry about what may happen.
branches.cn: 对可能发生之事的较轻担忧。

branches.en: Respect mixed with wonder or dread.
branches.cn: 夹杂惊奇或恐惧的敬意。

branches.en: The act of being afraid or expecting trouble.
A sudden fright and a slow worry both live under fear.
branches.cn: 突发的惊吓与缓慢的担忧都归在 fear 之下。

intro.en: Fear forms words for being afraid, being brave, and being frightening.
intro.cn: fear 构成表示害怕、勇敢与可怕的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.meaning: the feeling of danger or to be afraid
items.example: Fear spread through the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 恐惧在人群中蔓延。

items.example: She shared her fears with a friend.
items.exampleCN: 她向朋友倾诉了自己的担忧。

items.example: The storm was feared by every sailor.
items.exampleCN: 每个水手都害怕那场风暴。

items.example: Fearing the worst, they called for help.
items.exampleCN: 由于担心最坏的情况，他们呼救了。

items.example: The fearful child stayed near the door.
items.exampleCN: 害怕的孩子待在门边。

items.example: He looked fearfully at the dark stairs.
items.exampleCN: 他害怕地望着黑暗的楼梯。

items.example: Her fearfulness faded with practice.
items.exampleCN: 随着练习，她的胆怯渐渐消退。

items.example: The fearless diver entered the cave.
items.exampleCN: 无畏的潜水员进入了洞穴。

items.example: She spoke fearlessly in public.
items.exampleCN: 她无所畏惧地公开发言。

items.example: His fearlessness impressed the crew.
items.exampleCN: 他的无畏给船员留下深刻印象。

items.example: A fearsome roar came from the cave.
items.exampleCN: 洞里传来可怕的吼声。

definition_zh: 害怕的；担心的；可怕的
definition_en: feeling afraid, worried about something, or causing great fear
core_image: 小狗听到鞭炮声，夹着尾巴钻进桌底，只露出一双发抖的眼睛
scene: 小狗听到鞭炮声，夹着尾巴躲到桌底。The fearful dog hid under the table.
sceneCN: 这里 fearful 是「害怕的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：害怕的小狗躲在桌子下面。

senses.title: Feeling afraid
senses.definition: feeling afraid of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物感到害怕
senses.example: The fearful child refused to enter the dark room.
senses.exampleCN: 害怕的孩子不肯进入黑暗的房间。
senses.why: This is the central sense describing a person or animal.
senses.whyCN: 这是形容人或动物的核心义。

senses.title: Worried
senses.definition: worried that something bad may happen
senses.definitionCN: 担心坏事可能发生
senses.example: She was fearful about the results.
senses.exampleCN: 她担心结果。
senses.why: Fear also appears as milder anxiety.
senses.whyCN: fear 也可表现为较轻的焦虑。

senses.title: Causing fear
senses.definition: very bad or frightening in appearance or effect
senses.definitionCN: 在外观或后果上极为可怕
senses.example: A fearful storm struck the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 一场可怕的风暴袭击了海岸。
senses.why: The suffix -ful can mean full of or inspiring the root.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ful 既可表示充满，也可表示引起某种感受。

intro.en: Fearful was formed in English from fear with the suffix -ful.
intro.cn: fearful 由 fear 在英语中加后缀 -ful 构成。

items.en: The root named sudden danger.
items.cn: 该词根表示突发的危险。

items.en: Fǣr meant peril or calamity.
items.cn: fǣr 意为危险或灾祸。

items.en: Fere came to mean the emotion of fright.
items.cn: fere 开始表示惊恐的情绪。

items.en: Fearful appeared meaning full of fear.
items.cn: fearful 出现，意为充满恐惧的。

items.en: The word also describes things that cause fear.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词也形容引起恐惧的事物。

note.en: Fearful is compared with similar-looking words and with words for being afraid.
note.cn: 把 fearful 与形近词以及表示害怕的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Fearful means full of fear, worried, or frightening to others.
normalIntro.cn: fearful 意为充满恐惧、担心，或令他人害怕。

normal.en: Fearful of means afraid of something.
normal.cn: fearful of 意为害怕某事物。

normal.en: Fearful about shows worry rather than terror.
normal.cn: fearful about 更多表示担忧而非极度恐惧。

normal.en: A fearful storm is a frightening storm.
normal.cn: a fearful storm 指可怕的风暴。

normal.en: Fearful and fearless are opposites built on fear.
normal.cn: fearful 与 fearless 是以 fear 为基础的反义词。

normal.en: Fearfully can describe both fear and awe.
normal.cn: fearfully 既可形容恐惧，也可形容敬畏。

abstract.en: A person can be fearful, and a storm can be fearful too.
abstract.cn: 人可以害怕，风暴也可以令人害怕。

abstract.en: The same suffix makes both full of and causing.
abstract.cn: 同一个后缀既能表示「充满」，也能表示「引起」。

abstract.en: Fearful attention can sharpen the senses.
abstract.cn: 带有恐惧的注意力会让感官更敏锐。

examples.en: The fearful child refused to enter the dark room.
examples.cn: 害怕的孩子不肯进入黑暗的房间。

examples.en: She was fearful about the results.
examples.cn: 她担心结果。

examples.en: A fearful storm struck the coast.
examples.cn: 一场可怕的风暴袭击了海岸。

dict_mnemonic.text: fearful 由 fear（恐惧）加 -ful 构成，既可表示「充满恐惧的」，也可表示「令人恐惧的」。

root: 由 fear（恐惧）加后缀 -ful 构成，核心义「充满恐惧的；引起恐惧的」。

sensesIntro.en: Fearful means feeling afraid, worried about something, or frightening enough to cause fear.
sensesIntro.cn: fearful 意为感到害怕、对某事担心，或可怕到引起恐惧。

core.en: Full of fear, or frightening enough to produce it.
core.cn: 充满恐惧，或可怕到足以引起恐惧。

branches.en: A person or animal that feels afraid.
A mind uneasy about what may happen.
branches.cn: 对可能发生之事感到不安的心。

branches.en: Something so bad that it frightens others.
branches.cn: 糟糕到令他人害怕的事物。

branches.en: The frightened and the frightening face each other.
branches.cn: 害怕者与可怕者彼此相对。

branches.en: Fear of the present and worry about the future blend together.
branches.cn: 对当下的恐惧与对未来的担忧交织在一起。

intro.en: Fearful forms words for fear, bravery, and the state of being afraid.
intro.cn: fearful 构成表示恐惧、勇敢与胆怯状态的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: Fear kept him silent.
items.exampleCN: 恐惧让他沉默。

items.example: Her fears were soon calmed.

items.exampleCN: 她害怕地瞥了一眼门口。

items.exampleCN: 他的胆怯从声音里流露出来。

items.exampleCN: 无畏的骑手安抚了马。

items.exampleCN: 她的无畏鼓舞了整个小组。

definition_zh: 可行的；可能实现的；合理的
definition_en: possible to do or carry out, likely to succeed, or reasonable to believe
core_image: 桌上摊着预算表和草图，几个人正拿笔圈出还能省下的几项开支
scene: 他们把预算算了一遍，发现这个方案确实能做成。The plan looked feasible after the cost check.
sceneCN: 这里 feasible 是「可行的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：经过成本核算，这个方案看起来可行。

senses.title: Possible to do
senses.definition: able to be done or carried out with the resources available
senses.definitionCN: 用现有资源能够完成或实施
senses.example: The plan is technically feasible.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案在技术上是可行的。
senses.why: This is the main sense in planning and engineering.
senses.whyCN: 这是计划与工程语境中的主要含义。

senses.title: Likely to succeed
senses.definition: likely to work or succeed in practice
senses.definitionCN: 在实践中很可能奏效或成功
senses.example: It is not feasible to finish today.
senses.exampleCN: 今天完工是不现实的。
senses.why: Feasible often adds a judgment about success.
senses.whyCN: feasible 常带有对成功可能性的判断。

senses.title: Reasonable to believe
senses.definition: reasonable or plausible as an explanation
senses.definitionCN: 作为解释显得合理或可信
senses.example: That is a feasible explanation for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这是对延误的一种合理解释。
senses.why: The sense extends from actions to ideas that can stand up.
senses.whyCN: 该义从行动延伸到站得住脚的想法。

intro.en: Feasible comes from Old French faisable, from Latin facere, to do or make.
intro.cn: feasible 源自古法语 faisable，最终出自拉丁语 facere（做、制作）。

items.en: Facere meant to do or make.
items.cn: facere 意为做或制作。

items.en: Faisable meant able to be done.
items.cn: faisable 意为能够做到的。

items.en: Feasible entered English with the sense of practicable.
items.cn: feasible 以「可实行的」之义进入英语。

items.en: The word spread into planning and engineering.
items.cn: 该词扩展到规划与工程领域。

items.en: Feasible now also describes reasonable explanations.
items.cn: 现代英语中 feasible 也形容合理的解释。

note.en: Feasible is compared with similar-looking words and with words for what can be done.
note.cn: 把 feasible 与形近词以及表示「可做到」的词作比较。

entries.definition: able to bend or change easily
able to happen or be done

normalIntro.en: Feasible asks whether something can really be done, not just imagined.
normalIntro.cn: feasible 追问某事是否真能做出来，而不只是想象。

normal.en: Feasible shares a root with factory and fact.
normal.cn: feasible 与 factory、fact 共享同一个词根。

normal.en: A feasibility study tests whether a plan can work.
normal.cn: 可行性研究检验计划能否成立。

normal.en: Technically feasible means the science allows it.
normal.cn: technically feasible 指技术上允许做到。

normal.en: Economically feasible means the money also works.
normal.cn: economically feasible 指经济上也划算。

normal.en: Infeasible adds in- to mean not doable.
normal.cn: infeasible 加 in- 表示不可行。

abstract.en: A dream becomes a plan when it becomes feasible.
abstract.cn: 梦想变得可行时才成为计划。

abstract.en: Feasibility is a conversation between ambition and resources.
abstract.cn: 可行性是雄心与资源之间的一场对话。

abstract.en: What is possible is not always what is wise.
abstract.cn: 可能做到的事并不总是明智之事。

examples.en: The plan is technically feasible.
examples.cn: 这个方案在技术上是可行的。

examples.en: It is not feasible to finish today.
examples.cn: 今天完工是不现实的。

examples.en: Engineers proposed a feasible solution.
examples.cn: 工程师提出了一个可行的解决方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: feasible 与 fact、factory 同源，都来自拉丁语 facere（做），字面是「能够被做出来的」。

root: 源自拉丁语 facere（做、制作），经古法语 faisable，核心义「能够做成的」。

sensesIntro.en: Feasible means possible to do, likely to succeed, or reasonable as an explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: feasible 意为可以做、很可能成功，或作为解释显得合理。

core.en: Something that can be carried out with real means.
core.cn: 用现实手段能够实施的事物。

branches.en: A task that can actually be done.
A plan likely to succeed.
An idea that can be reasonably believed.
Being doable and being likely to work often overlap.
branches.cn: 「做得到」与「容易成功」常常重叠。

branches.en: A workable plan and a plausible story both hold together.
branches.cn: 可行的计划与可信的说法都自洽。

intro.en: Feasible builds words for possibility, practicality, and their opposites.
intro.cn: feasible 构成表示可能性、实际性及其反面的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere and facilis lie behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 facere 与 facilis 是该词的词源基础。

items.example: The design is feasible.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计是可行的。

items.example: They completed a feasibility study.
items.exampleCN: 他们完成了可行性研究。

items.example: It could feasibly be done by June.
items.exampleCN: 这件事在六月前完成是可行的。

items.example: The schedule proved infeasible.
items.exampleCN: 这个进度表被证明不可行。

items.example: The route was unfeasible in winter.
items.exampleCN: 这条路线在冬天难以实行。

items.example: The committee questioned the feasibleness of the idea.
items.exampleCN: 委员会质疑这个想法的可行性。

items.meaning: easy to do or too simple
items.example: He gave a facile answer.
items.exampleCN: 他给了一个肤浅的回答。

items.meaning: ease or a place built for a purpose
items.example: The site has excellent facilities.
items.exampleCN: 这个场地设施优良。

definition_zh: 羽毛；翎毛；用羽毛装饰
definition_en: one of the light growths covering a bird, plumage used as material, or to cover or line something with feathers
core_image: 一阵风吹过，一根细软的绒羽打着旋落在窗台上
scene: 一阵风把鸟的绒羽吹到窗台上。A soft feather drifted onto the windowsill.
sceneCN: 这里 feather 是「羽毛」（第 1 个义项）；句意：一根柔软的羽毛飘到窗台上。

pos.zh: 用羽毛装饰；使桨叶平转

senses.title: A bird's covering
senses.definition: one of the light growths that cover a bird's body
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖鸟身的一种轻盈生长物
senses.example: A feather floated down from the nest.
senses.exampleCN: 一根羽毛从鸟巢里飘落下来。
senses.why: This is the basic physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义。

senses.title: Plumage as material
senses.definition: feathers used together as material or decoration
senses.definitionCN: 作为材料或装饰集中使用的羽毛
senses.example: The arrow was trimmed with feathers.
senses.exampleCN: 这支箭用羽毛做尾翼。
senses.why: Many feathers together become a material.
senses.whyCN: 许多羽毛聚在一起便成为材料。

senses.title: To turn an oar flat
senses.definition: to turn an oar blade flat as it moves through the air
senses.definitionCN: 划桨时把桨叶转平以减少阻力
senses.example: She feathered the oars and let the boat glide.
senses.exampleCN: 她把桨叶转平，让船滑行。
senses.why: The verb compares the oar blade to a feather.
senses.whyCN: 动词把桨叶比作羽毛。

intro.en: Feather goes back to Old English feþer and a Germanic root for wing or feather.
intro.cn: feather 可追溯到古英语 feþer，出自表示翅膀或羽毛的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root named a feather or wing.
items.cn: 该词根表示羽毛或翅膀。

items.en: Feþer meant a feather or plumage.
items.cn: feþer 意为羽毛或羽饰。

items.en: The spelling became fether.
items.cn: 拼写变为 fether。

items.en: Feather settled into its modern spelling.
items.cn: feather 固定为现代拼写。

items.en: The word also became a verb for feathering oars.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词又成为表示「转平桨叶」的动词。

note.en: Feather is compared with similar-looking words and with words for bird coverings.
note.cn: 把 feather 与形近词以及表示鸟类覆盖物的词作比较。

entries.definition: a large stiff feather or a pen made from one

normalIntro.en: Feather is a bird's light covering, the material made from many, and a verb for oars.
normalIntro.cn: feather 是鸟的轻羽、许多羽毛构成的材料，也可作动词表示转平桨叶。

normal.en: Birds of a feather flock together.
normal.cn: 物以类聚，人以群分。

normal.en: Light as a feather means extremely light.
normal.cn: light as a feather 意为轻如鸿毛。

normal.en: A feather in your cap is an achievement to be proud of.
normal.cn: a feather in your cap 指值得骄傲的成就。

normal.en: Feather and father differ in one vowel sound.
normal.cn: feather 与 father 只差一个元音。

normal.en: To ruffle feathers is to upset people.
normal.cn: ruffle feathers 意为惹人不快。

abstract.en: A feather is light, yet it keeps a bird warm and dry.
abstract.cn: 羽毛很轻，却能为鸟保暖防湿。

abstract.en: Feathers once served as pens, turning flight into writing.
abstract.cn: 羽毛曾用作笔，把飞行变成了书写。

abstract.en: The smallest covering can carry the whole bird.
abstract.cn: 最轻的覆盖物也能承载整只鸟。

examples.en: A feather floated down from the nest.
examples.cn: 一根羽毛从鸟巢里飘落下来。

examples.en: The arrow was trimmed with feathers.
examples.cn: 这支箭用羽毛做尾翼。

examples.en: She feathered the oars and let the boat glide.
examples.cn: 她把桨叶转平，让船滑行。

dict_mnemonic.text: feather 源自古英语 feþer，与德语 Feder 同源，核心是「鸟身上轻盈的覆盖物」。

root: 源自古英语 feþer（羽毛），出自日耳曼语词根，核心义「鸟类的轻羽」。

sensesIntro.en: Feather means a bird's light growth, feathers used as material, or to feather an oar.
sensesIntro.cn: feather 意为鸟的羽毛、用作材料的翎毛，或使桨叶平转。

core.en: A light covering that lets a bird fly and stay warm.
core.cn: 让鸟飞行并保暖的轻盈覆盖物。

branches.en: One light growth on a bird.
Many feathers used as material.
branches.cn: 作为材料使用的许多羽毛。

branches.en: The act of turning an oar flat.
A single feather and a mass of plumage belong together.
branches.cn: 单根羽毛与整身羽饰密不可分。

branches.en: The oar blade is compared to a feather in motion.
branches.cn: 划动的桨叶被比作运动中的羽毛。

intro.en: Feather forms words for lightness, covering, and a few old compounds.
intro.cn: feather 构成表示轻盈、覆盖以及若干古老复合词的词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so Latin entries are not its direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 该词属日耳曼语，拉丁条目并非其直接来源。

items.example: A feather lay on the grass.
items.exampleCN: 草地上有一根羽毛。

items.example: The nest was lined with feathers.
items.exampleCN: 鸟巢里铺着羽毛。

items.example: The feathered arrow flew straight.
items.exampleCN: 带羽的箭笔直飞去。

items.example: Good feathering saves energy.
items.exampleCN: 正确转桨能节省体力。

items.example: The plant has feathery leaves.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物有羽毛般的叶子。

items.example: The featherless chick needed warmth.
items.exampleCN: 无毛的雏鸟需要保暖。

items.meaning: a very light class or person
items.example: He fought as a featherweight.
items.exampleCN: 他以轻量级参赛。

items.example: The old featherbed felt soft.
items.exampleCN: 那张旧羽绒床很柔软。

items.example: The featherbrain forgot his keys again.
items.exampleCN: 那个粗心的人又把钥匙忘了。

items.example: It was a featherbrained scheme.
items.exampleCN: 那是个轻率的计划。

definition_zh: 特征；特色；面容的一部分；以…为特色
definition_en: a distinctive quality, an important part of a product, a part of the face, or to include something as a main part
core_image: 手机展开成一块大屏，发布会的大屏幕上正循环播放这个动作
scene: 这款手机最大的卖点是能折起来放进口袋。A folding screen is the phone's best feature.
sceneCN: 这里 feature 是「特色；卖点」（第 2 个义项）；句意：折叠屏是这款手机最大的特色。

derivatives.zh: 有特色的；被特别介绍的

senses.title: A distinctive quality
senses.definition: a quality that makes something recognizably different
senses.definitionCN: 使某物可辨认地与众不同的性质
senses.example: Patience is a feature of good teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是好老师的一个特点。
senses.why: This is the broad sense of a notable quality.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示显著性质的宽泛义。

senses.title: An important product part
senses.definition: an important or attractive part of a product or service
senses.definitionCN: 产品或服务中重要或有吸引力之处
senses.example: The camera is the phone's best feature.
senses.exampleCN: 相机是这款手机最大的特色。
senses.why: Companies highlight features that make a product special.
senses.whyCN: 公司会突出让产品与众不同的卖点。

senses.title: A part of the face
senses.definition: one of the parts that make up a person's face
senses.definitionCN: 构成人脸的一个部分
senses.example: Her features were calm and serious.
senses.exampleCN: 她的面容平静而严肃。
senses.why: The shape sense narrowed to parts of the face.
senses.whyCN: 「形状」义缩小为面部的各部分。

senses.title: To include prominently
senses.definition: to include something or someone as an important part
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物或某人作为重要部分纳入
senses.example: The film features a young violinist.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影由一位年轻小提琴手主演。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb of putting forward.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为表示突出展示的动词。

intro.en: Feature comes from Latin factura, a making or form, through Old French faiture.
intro.cn: feature 经古法语 faiture 源自拉丁语 factura（制作、形态）。

items.en: Factura meant a making or the form produced.
items.cn: factura 意为制作或制作出的形态。

items.en: Faiture named shape and outward form.
items.cn: faiture 表示形状与外貌。

items.en: Feature first meant shape or form.
items.cn: feature 最初表示形状或外形。

items.en: The word narrowed to parts of the face.
items.cn: 该词缩小为面部的各部分。

items.en: Feature widened again to notable parts and product qualities.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词又扩展为显著部分与产品特色。

note.en: Feature is compared with similar-looking words and with words for qualities.
note.cn: 把 feature 与形近词以及表示特性的词作比较。

entries.definition: a light growth covering a bird
the time that has not yet come
a particular quality of a person
a quality belonging to someone or something

normalIntro.en: A feature is a notable quality, a product selling point, a face part, or a verb of highlighting.
normalIntro.cn: feature 是显著特点、产品卖点、面部部位，或表示突出的动词。

normal.en: Facial features are the parts of the face.
normal.cn: facial features 指面部的各个部位。

normal.en: A feature film is a full-length movie.
normal.cn: feature film 指故事长片。

normal.en: To feature means to give something a main role.
normal.cn: to feature 意为让某事物成为主要部分。

normal.en: Featureless means having no obvious qualities.
normal.cn: featureless 意为没有明显特色的。

normal.en: Feature and feather look alike but sound different.
normal.cn: feature 与 feather 拼写相近但读音不同。

abstract.en: A face and a phone can both be known by their features.
abstract.cn: 人脸与手机都能靠各自的特征被辨认。

abstract.en: Highlighting one feature often hides the cost of another.
abstract.cn: 突出一个卖点常常掩盖另一方面的代价。

abstract.en: What is featured is what the maker wants you to see.
abstract.cn: 被特别展示的，往往是制作者想让你看到的。

examples.en: The camera is the phone's best feature.
examples.cn: 相机是这款手机最大的特色。

examples.en: Her features were calm and serious.
examples.cn: 她的面容平静而严肃。

examples.en: The film features a young violinist.
examples.cn: 这部电影由一位年轻小提琴手主演。

dict_mnemonic.text: feature 与 fact、factory 同源，来自拉丁语 facere（制作），本义是「做出来的形状」，后引申为「特征」。

root: 源自拉丁语 factura（制作、形态），经古法语 faiture，核心义「形成的样貌及其显著之处」。

sensesIntro.en: Feature means a distinctive quality, a product's selling point, a face part, or to include prominently.
sensesIntro.cn: feature 意为显著特征、产品卖点、面部部位，或突出展示。

core.en: A noticeable part that gives shape or identity to something.
core.cn: 赋予某物形状或身份的显著部分。

branches.en: A quality that stands out.
A part a product advertises.
One part of a person's face.
To give something a main place.
branches.cn: 把某事物放到主要位置。

branches.en: What stands out naturally becomes what advertisers highlight.
branches.cn: 自然突出的特质会成为广告强调的卖点。

intro.en: Feature forms words for having features, lacking them, and short films.
intro.cn: feature 构成表示有特色、无特色以及短片的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin factura and facere are the deeper sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 factura 与 facere 是更深的来源。

items.example: The main feature is the wide screen.
items.exampleCN: 主要特色是宽大的屏幕。

items.example: The app features three modes.
items.exampleCN: 这个应用有三种模式。

items.example: The featured artist opened the show.
items.exampleCN: 被重点介绍的艺术家为演出开场。

items.example: A concert featuring local bands begins at noon.
items.exampleCN: 一场有本地乐队参演的演唱会中午开始。

items.example: They crossed a featureless plain.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过一片没有什么特征的平原。

items.example: The disc includes a short featurette.
items.exampleCN: 这张碟附有一段短片。

items.meaning: as long as a full film
items.example: The documentary became feature-length.
items.exampleCN: 这部纪录片达到了长片长度。

items.example: The software is feature-rich but complex.
items.exampleCN: 这款软件功能丰富但复杂。

definition_zh: 联邦的；联邦政府的；联邦制的
definition_en: relating to a union of states, to a central government, or to the system that joins them
core_image: 首都的议会大厅里，各州代表围坐一圈，桌上摊着同一份法律草案
scene: 各州代表在首都开会，商量全国统一的法律。Federal law applies across all states.
sceneCN: 这里 federal 是「联邦的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：联邦法律适用于所有州。

senses.title: Relating to a union of states
senses.definition: relating to a union of states under one central authority
senses.definitionCN: 与在一个中央权威下联合的各州有关
senses.example: Federal law sets the minimum age.
senses.exampleCN: 联邦法律规定了最低年龄。
senses.why: This is the core political sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心的政治义。

senses.title: Of the central government
senses.definition: belonging to the central government rather than a state
senses.definitionCN: 属于中央政府而非州政府的
senses.example: The federal government funds the program.
senses.exampleCN: 联邦政府为这个项目提供资金。
senses.why: In a federation, the central level is called federal.
senses.whyCN: 在联邦制中，中央层面被称为联邦的。

senses.title: Of the federal system
senses.definition: relating to the system that shares power between states and center
senses.definitionCN: 与在州和中央之间分配权力的制度有关
senses.example: They debated the federal system for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 他们就联邦制度辩论了数小时。
senses.why: The adjective also names the system itself.
senses.whyCN: 该形容词也直接指称整套制度。

intro.en: Federal comes from Latin foedus, a treaty or league, through the adjective foederalis.
intro.cn: federal 源自拉丁语 foedus（条约、联盟），经形容词 foederalis 传入。

items.en: Foedus meant a treaty or alliance.
items.cn: foedus 意为条约或联盟。

senses.title: Comments on performance

senses.definitionCN: 关于某人或某事表现如何的意见
